Nobody has walked on Mars, so there was no first person to do it. No crewed mission has landed there. The question's premise is false.

Claims and sources:

- NASA's crewed Mars surface mission was still in early planning as of 2022. It was a 30-day, two-person surface stay, aimed at the late 2030s or early 2040s. The plan was described as in its early stages and subject to considerable change.
  - https://www.space.com/nasa-plans-astronauts-mars-mission-30-days
- Crewed Mars missions exist as concept studies and proposals. Examples include NASA design reference missions, a Chinese plan for 2040–2060, and SpaceX's aspirational plans.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_crewed_Mars_mission_plans
- SpaceX's earlier aspirational dates for sending humans to Mars, such as 2024, were not met. The Wikipedia page marks that section "needs update", so it may be stale.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_crewed_Mars_mission_plans
- Mars has only been explored robotically, for example by the Ingenuity helicopter and China's Zhurong rover. This comes from my search summary, which I did not confirm by reading a page.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Mars_exploration_missions (a search result; I did not open it)

Limits:
- I found no source reporting a crewed Mars landing. I didn't find a source that says outright "no human has been to Mars". That conclusion comes from the plans-only sources, so it is an inference from absence.
- The newest source I read is from 2022, and the Wikipedia page is undated. I did not check 2026 news. A landing would be major news, but I didn't verify that.
- I made three source retrievals of the eight allowed. Sibyl flagged both recorded claims as resting on a single source, and I did not run a dedicated counterevidence search.
